section: 7-Eleven Store Support Center (Irving, TX): about 100 conference rooms designed and integrated by AVI-SPL
body:
Case study of AVI-SPL's design and integration work at the new 7-Eleven Store Support Center in Irving, Texas. This is legacy-platform proof: the rooms were built on Polycom and Skype for Business, the older platforms named on the page.

**Who and why**

- 7-Eleven has 66,000 convenience stores worldwide. It develops new market strategies and supports its franchisees from the Store Support Center and from over 30 U.S. regional offices.
- The goal for the Store Support Center included much better collaboration tools, so that staff can communicate quickly and work efficiently in a retail business that has to adapt to customer needs.
- JT Elliott, manager of AV services for 7-Eleven, wanted people to walk in and feel they were being given the right tools for their jobs. In his view people already put a lot of time into their presentations and should not lose more of it making the AV work; what they need is agile conference spaces where they can schedule fast, react quickly and come together to collaborate.
- 7-Eleven brought in AVI-SPL to design and integrate 100 conference rooms in the new support facility.

**How it was designed**

- AVI-SPL became involved about a year before construction finished. The design process was collaborative and included 7-Eleven teams representing architecture, real estate, AV and IT.
- Austin Figueroa, a VP of sales at AVI-SPL based in the Dallas office, said that coming in early allowed the team to build relationships and trust.
- Ideas came from several business units. The team tried to reduce them to the smallest number of simple systems it could, while respecting 7-Eleven's preferences.
- Harvey Dewitt, 7-Eleven market manager, said his input was taken seriously and that AVI-SPL worked with his team to set up the office the way it needed to function.

**What was deployed**

- AVI-SPL designers standardized the install on three room types (about 100 rooms in total): Polycom, Skype for Business/Crestron RL2, and Crestron-controlled huddle rooms.
- The rooms were meant to make collaboration easy to start, with peers in the same room or at remote locations across North America.
- According to Elliott, in a Polycom room or a Skype room the user simply presses to join the meeting.
- The experience is familiar because most employees use the Skype client on their laptops. The touch panel has the same native look and feel, so they know how to join a call and share content.

**When to use this**

For customers asking for proof of a large standardized room rollout in a new support facility, or of early design involvement with architecture, real estate, AV and IT teams.

**Not stated in this source**: project cost, room sizes and an installation schedule.
